task.title: Enable operator choice and judgment-based implementation placement
task.description:
## Outcome
Enable operator choice between direct implementation in the current checkout and the existing isolated Episode workflow. Stop treating every task implementation request as a command to invoke implement_task or to enter formal planning. Joe explicitly approved the routing behavior below and requested implementation ("make it so"). This is separate from PRIMECLAW-52, which must remain untouched.

## Agreed routing behavior
An explicit operator placement choice wins. "Here", "in this checkout", or "on main" means direct work in that checkout without implement_task, Episode allocation, or an Episode-only execute workflow. An explicit Episode request uses the existing implementation-readiness and isolated Episode lifecycle.
When placement is unspecified, use semantic judgment: a task clearly already planned, evidenced by appropriate native ticket status and a meaningful plan/design, defaults to an Episode; an obvious quick bug fix or easy small unplanned change defaults to direct implementation; a substantial task still in design that would benefit from formal planning requires one focused operator question before starting that workflow. Ambiguous or conflicting evidence also calls for a focused question, not an always-ask rule. In Design alone must not block a clearly small authorized direct change. Do not implement a rigid size/status classifier.

## Direct task lifecycle (operator decisions from grill-me)
Before editing implementation files for any authorized direct tracked change, including a quick fix, publish the exact task's native `In Progress` state. First verify the selected task, placement, and absence of a same-task active Episode. After required checks pass and the approved change is committed and pushed (or committed locally in a project with no remote), publish the task as `Done` without a separate approval solely for status. Honor any explicit review hold; this does not grant merge, deployment, or activation authority.

## Scope
Update plugin-injected routing guidance, managed entry skills, relevant project workflow/template guidance, and role wording so these paths agree. Preserve explicit placement through any requested planning and conditional implementation continuation; do not force "plan then implement here" into an Episode. Scope owner-Conversation implementation prohibitions and Episode identity/plan checks to managed Episode work, rather than all ordinary implementation. Direct execution uses ordinary supported native task CLI, tests, and Git operations; it creates no Episode resources or ownership record and does not borrow another role's authority. Keep this task-native; do not redesign retained version-1 specification lifecycle.

## Constraints and non-goals
Keep operator scope/implementation authority, exact task identity, provider-native task publication, existing Git/test safety, credential isolation, and all existing Episode ownership/terminal safeguards. Do not allow direct work to conflict with an active Episode bound to the same task or modify another owner's state; surface that conflict rather than adopting or bypassing it. Preserve EXPERT read-only boundaries. No new public tool, routing service, persisted mode state, ownership format, approval receipt, classifier framework, Prime Agent upstream change, or unrelated cleanup. Do not silently select another task. This implementation authorizes source changes and isolated candidate validation, not merge, user-global activation, restart, live migration, or cleanup of unrelated resources.

## Validation
Add proportional regression coverage for explicit direct/Episode choice, judgment-based defaults, substantial-unplanned/ambiguous ask-first cases, and placement surviving plan-then-implement. Show that direct instructions do not invoke Episode tools or require Episode identity/formal plan evidence, while existing Episode admission and ownership protections remain intact. Use Docker-only candidate validation and mandatory Tier 1 --probe after plugin source changes. Do not use host/user-global candidate apply/check/probes.

Preserve that conditional authority across phases; do not ask again solely because a phase ended. Product/scope changes, new source merges, destructive data repair, and customized-asset replacement retain their normal explicit decisions.

PRIMECLAW-45 is merged, active Done, and cleaned up. It explicitly excluded activation and must not be reopened. Its compatibility implementation pins unmodified upstream v1.55.3 commit `0cf4fdbc70020327f4366a29d3f405f83d180301`. ## Required rollout behavior

Build the merged exact v1.55.3 source using the supported pinned toolchain and existing build/compiled smoke interfaces. Establish the exact source, artifact identity/hash, version, installation destination, and supported command resolution. Preserve the accepted fallback until the reviewed replacement is proven; report failed or uncertain writes by inspecting actual state rather than blindly retrying. Do not print or obtain credentials, alter upstream source, or patch Prime Agent.

Activate the accepted Backlog artifact and coherent prime-claw user-global plugin generation through their supported installation paths, from canonical primary main at the deployment boundary. Candidate plugin development/testing remains Docker-only; no candidate host apply/check or second Prime Agent daemon. If narrow rollout tooling/docs changes are needed, deliver them through the normal isolated Episode, validation, review, and operator-controlled merge before deploying merged source. An Episode must not activate a candidate globally. Preserve unrelated global files/configuration and avoid project/global duplicate plugin discovery.

A global binary swap alone is insufficient. Inventory the relevant installed global guidance and discoverable prime-claw-managed project workflow assets using supported project/asset evidence. Bound discovery to known managed/registered project contexts; do not crawl or mutate arbitrary home-directory repositories. Distinguish ordinary Backlog projects, initialized prime-claw projects, customization/override conflicts, active or uncertain Episode snapshots, and unrelated projects. Establish and document the supported project-upgrade/reconciliation boundary. Reconcile safe untouched assets only in the selected prime-claw project through the existing initializer; preserve customized/unknown bytes, index state, task history, and live-generation resources. Coordinate other projects through their actual owners or report exact operator actions, not silent cross-project writes. Do not accept/reset overrides or overwrite customized assets without a separate explicit content decision.

Account for removed `task complete`/`task_complete`, legacy `completed/` versus canonical `archive/tasks/`, status-derived closure, archive identity reservation/read-only behavior, ordering/pagination, and unattended inputs. Legacy completed storage remains readable and does not imply a universal data rewrite. Use supported non-mutating native doctor inspection for each affected project that can be safely inspected; report unavailable evidence rather than assuming health. Never run `doctor --fix`, renumber/delete/relocate records, switch providers, or migrate real data under this rollout authority. Preserve the accepted archived-draft physical-byte/history/collision policy; unavailable archived-draft native view alone is not a new blocker.

Before coordinated restart, safely account for running/queued/unfinished work and explicitly owned descendants through actual owner/session evidence. Do not force-stop foreign work or infer ownership from CWD. Preserve every resource the old loaded generation may read. Coordinate the one full restart with Joe/the owning maintenance coordinator through supported public interfaces; do not use `/reload`, copy success, a fresh probe, or elapsed time as cutover proof. Existing schedules stay unchanged unless separately authorized.

After restart, prove exact installed artifact and plugin generation through successful live UAT in resumed owning Conversation, its exact Episode where applicable, and a designated ordinary project session. Exercise representative real native task/history and workflow behavior at the actual installed boundary without modifying unrelated production tasks/projects. Report any unsupported interface or unsafe active stale workflow as a blocker, not completed rollout. Inactive projects with unresolved customization must be explicitly identified as requiring owner/operator upgrade, not represented as upgraded. Document acceptance scope and any real deployment limitations.

Send the Backlog.md Expert exact published source/build/install/restart/UAT evidence and the affected-project/operator-action inventory. Only that Expert advances its own latest-stable pointer after verification.

## Non-goals

No new project manager/framework, parallel task authority, custom allocator/parser/index, global compliance database, broad refactor, upstream/Prime Agent patch, new sandbox rollout, mass repository mutation, blanket doctor fix, schedule changes, or reopening/completing PRIMECLAW-45 again. Reuse its unchanged compatibility/build/test evidence within stated limits, with fresh validation for changed and activated surfaces. Keep failed and incomplete histories distinct from passing proof. The native task remains the specification and living plan, not a new .ralph bundle.

## Operator correction: critical recovery-policy bug fix

Joe explicitly clarified: “That file should be committed as a critical change. That widening was a bug fix!” The installed `global-oversee-episode` policy is therefore the operator-selected critical source correction, not an optional customization to settle with an accepted override. Preserve its verified pre-work model/runtime-interruption recovery path and existing exact-owner, delivery/effects, idle, and explicit new-continuation authorization safeguards. Bring that exact correction into canonical plugin source, add focused regression evidence, commit and push it through the isolated Episode workflow, and obtain normal operator-controlled source merge acceptance before global rollout. Do not revert the fix or mark it an accepted override instead of landing it. Preserve the installed bytes while source acceptance is pending. A prerequisite source-fix slice is not completion of this whole activation task: retain active task/Episode/resources until the full rollout and UAT succeed. No activation, restart, or terminal cleanup follows merely from committing the fix.

task.description:
## Required migration scope — operator clarification
Joe explicitly clarified: "We only need to migrate the current state of the ticket from beads to backlog!" This supersedes earlier wording that treated importing full source history or lossless revision archives as a requirement.

Migrate each ticket's current readable content and supported metadata: title, description, acceptance criteria, current plan/design and notes, current lifecycle status/close information, priority, type, labels, assignee, parent/dependency relationships, and actual existing ticket comments. Preserve meaningful current fields through corresponding native Backlog fields or concise labeled readable text when no equivalent exists. Actual authored comments are ticket content; Dolt revision snapshots, database events, and old field versions are not.

Do NOT migrate per-ticket Dolt revision history, old ticket snapshots, database event streams, base64 export packages, or archive blobs into Backlog tasks, comments, documents, or a newly invented archival destination. Do not merely move the encoded data elsewhere: importing it is unnecessary. Do not collect full per-ticket revision/event histories as a prerequisite to migrating current state. JSON is acceptable internal transport; it is not a reason to embed encoded source archives into human-facing task Markdown. Do not duplicate whole-store catalogs/memory snapshots inside each ticket. Existing history already held by the destination need not be rewritten or deleted.

## Recovery identity guarantee
Unfinished import records do not have a stable Backlog-ID guarantee. An operator-authorized recovery may recreate records proven to be generated by the interrupted import, unfinished, and unmodified by users. Original Backlog records, IDs, configuration, and history remain protected. Records with user changes are not disposable. Recovery must leave one complete verified import per source ticket, not duplicate or incomplete destination tickets; this does not require a fully resumable importer.

## Cancellation behavior
Ordinary supported cancellation promptly stops further migration/provider writes without force-shutting down the Prime Agent runtime. Preserve partial destination data and the evidence needed to explain the stopped state. Cancellation does not automatically remove import records, roll back layout changes, retire the source, restart the import, or perform cleanup. Report what actually remains and which provider is authoritative; later cleanup or recovery requires an explicit instruction and the preservation/disposability rules above.

## Current defects and impact
During the first approved ralph-pva migration, the worker stopped without a result after writing 146 task files. All were generated by the import; the last provenance package had only 58 of 72 chunks. About 90 MB and 3812 native comment writes accumulated over 97 minutes. Beads remained intact and authoritative; no completion receipt existed. Same-revision retry failed before cutover with `source task history is not clean: ?? tasks/`, because replay requires a clean published destination and a full receipt rather than handling pre-receipt interruption.

Joe authorized deleting only the disposable partial `.backlog/` and generated layout projection, leaving Beads, the original `backlog/`, and the published bootstrap branch intact, then retrying. He subsequently deliberately aborted that recovery with `prime-agent shutdown --force` because ordinary interruption did not stop it and it had run over half an hour. The tool reported `append Backlog provenance to TASK-52: backlog command: command/capture failed (status=1, nativeStatus=null, signal=SIGTERM)`. Read-only inspection then found 59 task files, 1671 encoded chunks, and 39,760,679 bytes. This SIGTERM reflects operator shutdown; the earlier interruption cause remains unknown. No restart is authorized by this task update.

The unnecessary encoding is implemented by `backlogSourcePackage` (current data plus history/events/provenance and repeated source context), `chunkComment` (base64 in 24000-character pieces), and one separate `backlog task edit --comment` process per piece. This directly contributes to unreadability and runtime. The correct scope is current-state migration, not a more efficient way to archive all revisions. PRIMECLAW-50's former output-buffer defect is already fixed and is not this requirement error.

## Existing destination preservation and layout
The project also has three original `backlog/` records (RPVA-1, RPVA-2, and a distinct archived RPVA-2) plus `backlog/config.yml.pre-migration`, parked under an earlier authorized workaround. Fresh preparation treats that parked store as absent: the records remain physically preserved but are not consolidated into selected `.backlog/`. Restoring its config alone hits the exact lifecycle capability gate. Preserve existing records/configuration and distinct same-ID archive/live records without renumbering or omission.

Migration may add statuses needed by imported tickets when they are missing from the existing Backlog destination configuration. Retain existing statuses and unrelated settings; do not replace customization or demand one exact status list/order. This permission applies to Backlog only, not the retiring Beads source. Preserve and reconcile the known parked configuration under the same rule.

Native Backlog discovers `.backlog/config.yml` without a root link. Prime Claw creates `backlog.config.yml -> .backlog/config.yml` and adds `/.backlog/` to .gitignore; it does not ignore the root link. The published task-history bootstrap e48f9069d1c074b20129443a4df8371b5ac80951 has only TASKS.md/config.yml, and a disposable fixture proved it reusable after local rollback.

## Evidence and authority
The approved source capture was capture-sha256:feab12062b10e7b369f65cf30829a4053fb26bc073e5ab04ea344b5575327201: 406 tickets, 57 open/unclosed, 349 closed, zero active owners. That historical capture is evidence, not a requirement to retain its revision archive or permission to resume now.

Private evidence: `/Users/jlanders/gitlab_local/ralph-pva/reports/prime-claw/migration-rollback-investigation-2026-11-04.json`, `migration-operator-aborted-2026-11-04.json`, and disposable fixtures under `/tmp/ralph-migration-rollback-investigation-20261104/`. Do not copy raw private histories into this ticket.

Joe previously requested logging this bug without blocking the recovery attempt on its fix, then explicitly interrupted migration. Latest instruction here is to update this bug with current-state-only scope. No implementation, migration restart, cleanup, global installation, or Prime Agent source change is authorized by this update. Source stays authoritative until successful current-state destination verification/publication and separately applicable cutover authority.
